newsitem.title: GERMANY: Severe weather seen boosting German feeds prices.
newsitem.headline: Severe weather seen boosting German feeds prices.

text.p: Severe winter weather is adding to costs in the German feeds sector, and producers may need to impose surcharges, industry association FFMI said.
Transport costs had risen on waterways, and alternatives such as road and rail were expensive, it said.
"Higher procurement prices will have to result in higher compound feed prices ex-plant," an FFMI official said.
"This will also be necessary because the logistics problems coincide with firm global feeds prices and low consumer cover."
Meals and imported protein-rich grain substitutes were most affected but the transport of some domestic beet pulp and feed grain had also been disrupted.
FFMI declined to specify the extent of likely price rises.
The Rhine remained navigable, but tributaries and nearby canals had frozen, hampering barge movements, FFMI said.
Waterways including the Mittellandkanal, the Dortmund-Ems canal, the river Main, parts of the Neckar and Moselle rivers and the Main-Danube canal were also closed off.
The movement of raw materials from southeast Europe was affected.
Dutch waterways were also badly hit, blocking supplies to northern Germany.
The barge industry association BDB said last Friday that two thirds of its 3,000 vessels were icebound.
FFMI represents Germany's large compound feed producers accounting for more than 50 percent of the industry's total output of 19.06 million tonnes in 1995/96.
